<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **118** documentable anchor(s).

**30** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bafcdfe5ca9dbc1697ce4044f2bdd58066f6a5b7`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bafcdfe5ca9dbc1697ce4044f2bdd58066f6a5b7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `45860e1e08a4ebc48dbd48e43641f42af8ede4d7` — the merge of head `45207d625d7d8aaf3cbc9d22234674c868ac5bcc` into base `bafcdfe5ca9dbc1697ce4044f2bdd58066f6a5b7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 45860e1e08a4ebc48dbd48e43641f42af8ede4d7 && git checkout 45860e1e08a4ebc48dbd48e43641f42af8ede4d7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bafcdfe5ca9dbc1697ce4044f2bdd58066f6a5b7 45207d625d7d8aaf3cbc9d22234674c868ac5bcc && git checkout -B drift-repro bafcdfe5ca9dbc1697ce4044f2bdd58066f6a5b7 && git merge --no-ff 45207d625d7d8aaf3cbc9d22234674c868ac5bcc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bafcdfe5ca9dbc1697ce4044f2bdd58066f6a5b7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bafcdfe5ca9dbc1697ce4044f2bdd58066f6a5b7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位 ACCEPT · head `45207d625d7d8aaf3cbc9d22234674c868ac5bcc`

#30020 E6 PR B (`Refs #30020`): the body of `ObjectQL#update` moves into its own facet, `engine-update.ts`, written by the codemod's members pass (`--members update --write`, R11 from #32018). `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none`, `@objectstack/objectql` patch. One commit on `main` at eb66b74f (#32018), no merge.

- **The move.** `engine.ts` goes from 8692 to 6597 lines. `update` stays on the class as a one-call stub that keeps its signature and docblock: `UpdateFacet.update.call(updateHost.of(this), …)`. `engine-update.ts` is 2253 lines. `engine-facet-hosts.ts` gains the `UpdateHost` import and `updateHost`, both in sorted place. Where the body handed the engine itself on, it now reads the same engine through the host's `facade` entry. That is why the facade-delegation registry's `update` row ("state-owning: bare-this … stays on the class") no longer holds and is deleted (7 rows to 6).
- **Forced re-points, each with its gate (seat rulings, as for E5).**
  - The system-context census row `engine.ts#update` (4 calls, rows 19 and 20) now reads `engine-update.ts#update`. It was regenerated, not hand-edited.
  - #22474 (f): the parity test reads `engine-update.ts` too, so the write side's `evaluateValidationRules` calls are still compared against the preview.
  - ADR-0020 line 52: the link text and href point to `engine-update.ts#validateRecord`, with the wording unchanged.
- **Evidence (thread report 6757373197).**
  - objectql suite 583 files / 12016 tests, equal to base.
  - Dogfood 445 files (3 skipped) and 3689 tests (42 skipped), VERDICT 0.
  - Full build VERDICT 0, and the objectql `.d.ts` output is byte-identical to base.
  - Codemod undo proof `--members --verify --base eb66b74f` exit 0, and self-test 250 cases in 15 batteries.
  - All 111 dispatch gates exit 0. Lint clean.
  - The seat did not rerun the undo proof: this checkout has no `node_modules`, and the run stopped at its prerequisite (exit 3, nothing measured).

Landing: this PR is about 4,500 changed lines (a mechanical move) on a Tier H path, so it stays draft until a GOVERNED_APPROVERS approval (os-zhuang or hotlong). The seat makes no ready or queue move before that. CI on this head is still running; after the approval, the seat lands it once CI is all green and K is checked. When it merges, the landed record goes on #30020, and the card stays open.
